MemberNote.description:
A note as the member it is about sees it. Only shared notes ever reach this model, so it has
no flag, and no author: the member needs neither.
MemberNote.title: MemberNote

MemberReport.description: All a member ever gets of a report: the summary.
MemberReport.title: MemberReport

ParticipantHit.description: A search result: just enough to pick the person. Never an email.
ParticipantHit.title: ParticipantHit

ReportIn.description:
The whole report. A field that is left out is cleared (this is a PUT, a full replace).

`notes` is the exception: left out, the session's existing notes stay as they are (so fixing the
summary cannot wipe them); a list means exactly these notes for this session, which adds,
changes and removes (`[]` removes them all).
ReportIn.title: ReportIn

RsvpCounts.description: How many people chose each plan. Counts only: never who.
RsvpCounts.title: RsvpCounts

SeriesPatch.description:
A field that is left out stays unchanged; `capacity: null` makes the sessions unlimited.
Anything else (weekday, dates, class type) is refused with 422: end the series and make a new one.
SeriesPatch.title: SeriesPatch

SeriesSessionOut.description: One coming class of a series, with how many people said they are going (a count, never who).
SeriesSessionOut.title: SeriesSessionOut

SessionDetail.description:
One session with what a screen needs to show it: names instead of ids, and the caller's
own plan and own attendance (`my_attended`: true, false, or null when nothing is recorded; kept
apart from the plan, so someone can have attended without ever answering). `rsvp_counts` is for
coaches and owners; a member gets null, so nobody learns what the others chose, not even as a
total. `seats_left` is the one number every member gets: free
seats in a booking class with a seat limit, null when there are no seats to count.
SessionDetail.title: SessionDetail

SessionListItem.description:
A session as the schedule lists it: the caller's own plan too (`going`, `maybe`,
`not_going`, `waitlist`, or null when they have not answered), so a screen can ask for answers
without opening every class. The same fact as `SessionDetail.my_rsvp`.
SessionListItem.title: SessionListItem

SessionPatch.description:
A field that is left out stays unchanged; `preview: null` clears the preview and
`capacity: null` makes the session unlimited.
SessionPatch.title: SessionPatch

StaffNote.description: A note as staff see it: everything, including who wrote it and whether it is shared.
StaffNote.title: StaffNote

post.description:
Exchange email + password for tokens.

Returns a short-lived access token (JWT, 15 min) to send as `Authorization: Bearer ...`, and
a long-lived refresh token (30 days). Any failure (unknown email, wrong password, account
without a password) gives the same `401 invalid_credentials`.

Log out: end this login by revoking the refresh token's whole family (the token itself and
any it was rotated into or from), so none of them can be used again. Other devices' logins are
not affected.

Send the refresh token in the body; no Bearer header is needed, since the access token has
often expired by now. Always `204` for a well-formed request, including unknown or already
revoked tokens. The access token stays valid until it expires, so the client should discard it.

Trade a refresh token for a new access token and a new refresh token.

Send the refresh token in the body; no Bearer header is needed, since the access token has
expired. The old refresh token is used up (revoked and replaced), so the client must store
the new one. Unknown, expired and already-used tokens all give the same
`401 invalid_refresh_token`.

Presenting an already-used token again counts as theft: the whole login (every token of that
device) is revoked and the user must log in again. This includes two simultaneous refreshes
with the same token, so clients must send one refresh at a time. Reuse is only noticed when the
old token is presented; a thief who refreshes first and is never contradicted stays signed in
until the tokens expire.

get.description:
The class types of the studio named by `X-Tenant-Id`, ordered by name. Any member.

Archived ones are hidden unless `?include_archived=true`.

schema.title: Response List Class Types Class Types Get

post.description:
Create a class type in the studio named by `X-Tenant-Id`. Owner only.

The studio comes from the verified header, never from the body. `attendance_mode` defaults to
`rsvp`; `booking` needs the studio's booking module (`403 module_disabled`). A name the studio
already has, in any letter case and even on an archived type, is `409 class_type_name_taken`.

put.description:
Rename a class type of this studio, and optionally change its attendance mode. Owner only.

An omitted `attendance_mode` leaves the mode as it is; switching to `booking` needs the booking
module (`403 module_disabled`). A name another class type of the studio has is
`409 class_type_name_taken` (renaming to its own name, or only changing its case, is fine).

A class type of another studio gets the same `404 class_type_not_found` as one that does not
exist, so ids cannot be probed.

post.description:
Hide a class type and stop new sessions from using it. Owner only; repeating is fine (200).

Existing sessions, reports and notes are untouched. Another studio's class type gets the same
`404 class_type_not_found` as a missing one.
Make an archived class type active again. Owner only; repeating is fine (200).

delete.description:
Delete the logged-in user's own account, confirmed with their current password.

This cannot be undone. Everything that identifies them is erased or anonymized in one
transaction (see `app/deletion.py` for exactly what), and every login of theirs stops working
at once. A wrong password is `403 invalid_password`; an account without a password cannot be
confirmed yet (`409 reauthentication_unavailable`; Google/Apple accounts, step 53); the only
owner of a studio that still has other members gets `409 transfer_ownership_first`.

get.description:
The logged-in user's profile and the studios they belong to, with their role in each.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`; otherwise `401`.

Search the studio's participants by name, for coaches and owners (a member gets
`403 insufficient_role`).

`q` matches anywhere in the name, ignoring letter case; `%` and `_` in it are ordinary
characters, not wildcards. An empty `q` lists the first names alphabetically, so a picker has
something to show. At most `limit` results (default 20, at most 50): narrow `q` to find
someone else, there is no next page. Only this studio's participants, by name and never email.
A deleted account (its participant is renamed "Deleted user") is left out; a participant
without an account (a kid, step 47) is kept.
ponytail: anyone with a participant row is searchable, member or not; filter by membership
when members can be removed (step 50b).

The notes written about a participant, newest first. What you get depends on your role:

- **Coach or owner:** every note about any participant of the studio (any coach reads all
  notes), with who wrote each and whether it is shared.
- **Member:** only their own participant, and only the notes a coach shared with them, without
  author or flag. The filter is in the query, so a private note is never even fetched.

A participant of another studio, a missing one, and (for a member) anyone but themselves all
get the same `404 participant_not_found`, so ids cannot be probed. A member with nothing shared
gets `200 []`, which looks the same as having no notes at all.
ponytail: no pagination yet; the timeline (step 32) brings cursor pagination.

schema.title: Response List Notes Participants  Participant Id  Notes Get

get.description:
The classes a participant is connected to, newest first (upcoming ones first), a page at a
time: pass the previous response's `next_cursor` to continue (`null` = the last page).

- **Coach or owner:** any participant of the studio. A class appears when the participant has
  an RSVP or attendance row for it, or a note. Every note is shown with its author (id and name)
  and whether it is shared, and so is the summary of any class that has a report.
- **Member:** only their own participant, otherwise `404 participant_not_found` (the same as
  for an id that does not exist). A class appears only through their own RSVP or attendance
  row, or a note shared with them, so a class with nothing but a private note never shows up
  (even an empty entry would reveal that such a note exists). Only shared notes are shown, and
  the summary only for classes they attended (`member_visible_summaries`).

The page is found by position (`starts_at`, `id`) and not by counting rows (`OFFSET`), so it
stays correct when new classes appear while someone scrolls, and it costs the same on page 50
as on page 1. A malformed `cursor` is `422 invalid_cursor`.

schema.title: Response Timeline Participants  Participant Id  Timeline Get

get.description:
The classes starting in `[from, to)` whose report the caller may write, newest first. A
coach gets their own classes, an owner every class of the studio (the rule of `PUT
/sessions/{id}/report`); a member gets `403 insufficient_role`.

Only classes that have started and were not cancelled are listed, because those are the ones
that route accepts (`409 session_not_started`, `409 session_cancelled` otherwise). The range
follows the schedule's rules: `from` included, `to` not, at most 62 days (`422 invalid_range`,
`422 range_too_long`). The class type's name and whether a report exists come from joins, so a
long list costs no more round trips than a short one; `has_earlier` is one more `EXISTS` query.
The studio's series: an owner sees all of them, a coach only their own.

post.description:
Create a series in the studio named by `X-Tenant-Id`. Owner only (`403 insufficient_role`).

The class type and coach follow the rules of `POST /sessions`. `first_date` must fall on
`weekday` (`422 first_date_not_on_weekday`). The first four weeks of sessions are created with it.

delete.description:
Remove a series and all its sessions completely: for one created by mistake. Owner only;
404 if it is not in this studio.

All or nothing: if any of its sessions has anything recorded on it (an RSVP, a booking,
attendance, a report or a note) it is `409 series_has_history` and nothing is deleted. Use
`end` for a series that has really run.

get.description:
One series: 404 if it is not in this studio, 403 `not_your_series` if a coach (not an
owner) is not its coach.

patch.description:
Change the rule and every future session that follows it. Owner only.

Only sessions that are still to come, scheduled and not changed by hand follow the rule: past
and cancelled ones, and ones whose times, coach or capacity someone changed, are left as they
are (`sessions_kept` counts the last kind). A new start time keeps each session on its own
date, in the studio's timezone. A new coach must be staff (`422 invalid_coach`); a start time
that lands on an instant another session of the series already has is `409 session_time_clash`
and nothing is changed. Raising the capacity lets waiting people in, like editing one session.

post.description:
Stop a series from today (the studio's date). Owner only.

`last_date` becomes today (never later than it already was), so no more sessions are
generated. Everything that already happened is untouched. Sessions of later dates that are
still scheduled go: the ones nobody RSVP'd to are deleted, the ones with an RSVP are
cancelled so those people see it. Today's class stays, and already cancelled ones are left
as they are. A series whose `first_date` is still ahead gets `409 series_not_started` (it
never ran: that is a mistake to delete). Repeating it changes nothing (200, zeros).

Create the sessions the series is missing up to its horizon (four weeks from today, or
`last_date`). Owner only; 404 `series_not_found` if it is not in this studio. Repeating it
creates nothing new.

get.description:
The series' sessions that have not started yet, earliest first, cancelled ones included
(`status`), each with its `going` count. Read by whoever may read the series: an owner, or the
coach who teaches it (`403 not_your_series` for another coach; 404 if it is not in this studio).

schema.title: Response List Series Sessions Series  Series Id  Sessions Get

get.description:
The studio's sessions that start in `[from, to)`, earliest first, each with the caller's own
plan (`my_rsvp`, null when unanswered). Any member.

Both times need an offset. `from` is included and `to` is not, so back-to-back ranges neither
overlap nor miss a session. Invalid ranges get `422 invalid_range` (`to` not after `from`) or
`422 range_too_long` (over 62 days).

post.description:
Create a session in the studio named by `X-Tenant-Id`. Coach or owner.

A coach can only create their own sessions (`403 not_your_session` if they name someone
else); an owner can name any coach or owner of the studio (`422 invalid_coach` otherwise).
Times are stored in UTC. A class type of another studio gets `404 class_type_not_found`; an
archived one gets `422 class_type_archived`.

delete.description:
Remove a session completely, as if it had never been made: for a class created by mistake.
Owner only; 404 if it is not in this studio.

Refused while anything is recorded on it (`409 session_has_history`: an RSVP, a booking,
attendance, a report or a note; cancel it instead) and when it belongs to a series
(`409 session_in_series`: the next `extend` would just recreate it; cancel it, or delete or end
the series). The database's foreign keys refuse the same deletes, so a record written at the
last moment is a 409 too, never a half-deleted session.

get.description:
One session of this studio, with its class type's name, the coach's name, the caller's own
RSVP and attendance, the seats left (booking classes with a limit) and, for coaches and owners, how many chose
each plan. Any member.

The coach's name is visible to every member; their email never is. `my_rsvp` is the caller's
own plan (`going`, `not_going`, `maybe`, `waitlist`) or null; `my_attended` is whether they
themselves said they came (true, false, or null when not recorded), a separate fact from the
plan, and never anyone else's. A session of another studio gets
the same `404 session_not_found` as one that does not exist, so ids cannot be probed.

patch.description:
Change a session's preview, times or coach. The owner edits any session, a coach only their own.

Only the fields in the body change. Changing the coach is owner-only (`403 insufficient_role`)
and the new coach must be staff of the studio (`422 invalid_coach`). The resulting times must
still satisfy start < end (`422 invalid_times`). A cancelled session gets `409 session_cancelled`.

post.description:
Record whether someone actually came (`attended`), as opposed to their RSVP plan.

Members record their own. An owner can record anyone's on any session, a coach anyone's on
sessions they teach (`403 not_your_session` otherwise); a member naming someone else gets
`403 insufficient_role`. The person must be in this studio (`404 participant_not_found`).
Allowed from 15 minutes before the session starts (`409 checkin_not_open` before that). A
member can record it until 24 hours after the session ends (`409 checkin_closed` after that);
coaches and owners have no end. Not on a cancelled session (`409 session_cancelled`). Sending it again
changes the answer and refreshes `confirmed_at`. A session of another studio gets
`404 session_not_found`.

get.description:
Who came to a session, for coaches and owners (a member gets `403 insufficient_role`).

Everyone whose attendance is recorded as `attended: true`, by name (never email), with or
without an RSVP: someone who walked in and was marked present is here, someone who said
"going" and was not marked is not. `attended: false` and "not recorded" are left out. Any
coach reads any class's list, like the RSVP list and the reports. A cancelled session can still
be read. A session of another studio gets the same `404 session_not_found` as a missing one.

schema.title: Response List Attendees Sessions  Session Id  Attendees Get

post.description:
Cancel a session. The owner cancels any, a coach only their own. Repeating it is fine (200).

The session stays (reports and notes point at it) with `status: cancelled`.

get.description:
Read the report of a session. What you get depends on your role:

- **Coach or owner:** the whole report (any coach reads all reports) with its notes and their
  sharing flags, in the shape the `PUT` returns. `404 session_not_found` for a session of
  another studio, `404 report_not_found` when it has no report yet.
- **Member:** only the `summary`, and only for a session they attended. In every other case
  (no report, no summary, did not attend, attendance `false` or not recorded, a session of
  another studio or none at all) the same `404 report_not_found`, so a member cannot tell
  them apart.

schema.title: Response Read Report Sessions  Session Id  Report Get

put.description:
Write the report of a session, with a private note per attendee, or replace what is there.
The owner writes any session's, a coach only their own sessions' (`403 not_your_session`).

There is one report per session, and a PUT replaces all of it: a field that is not sent is
cleared. Notes are different: left out they stay, a list replaces them (see `ReportIn`). The
report and its notes are saved in one transaction, so a rejected note means nothing is saved.
A report needs text in at least one field or at least one note (`422 empty_report`); a note
about someone who is not in this studio is `422 participant_not_found`. A cancelled session
gets `409 session_cancelled`, one that has not started yet `409 session_not_started`; a session of another studio `404 session_not_found`. The author
and time are those of the latest save. Attendees will only see `summary` (step 31).

Set the caller's own plan for a session: going, not_going or maybe. Any member.

An upsert: the first call creates the RSVP and later calls change it, so repeating a request is
fine. It is only an intention; attendance after the class is a separate step. The RSVP belongs
to the caller's participant in this studio, never to one named by the client. A session of
another studio gets `404 session_not_found`; a cancelled one gets `409 session_cancelled`.

In a booking-mode class (module on) a `going` takes one of `capacity` seats. When all are taken
the answer is still 200 but the status is `waitlist`: the person waits in line, and the earliest
waiting person is promoted to `going` when a seat frees up. `maybe` and `not_going` never take
a seat (and take you off the waitlist), and repeating `going` keeps your seat or your place.

get.description:
Who is coming to a session, for coaches and owners (a member gets `403 insufficient_role`).

One entry per person with a plan, by name and never by email: going first, then the waiting
list in queue order, then maybe, then not going; by name inside each of the others. People with
no plan (attendance recorded without an RSVP) are left out. A cancelled session can still be
read. A session of another studio gets the same `404 session_not_found` as a missing one.

The waiting list is ordered as `promote_waitlist` picks people (`waitlisted_at`, ties by
participant id), so position 1 is who gets the next free seat.
ponytail: no pagination, the list is bounded by the studio's size; add a cursor if a studio
ever has thousands of RSVPs on one class.

schema.title: Response List Rsvps Sessions  Session Id  Rsvps Get

get.description:
The coaches and owners of this studio, by name. Owner only: nobody else may name a coach.
No emails: the picker needs only a name to show and an id to send.

The studio named by `X-Tenant-Id`, with its timezone and the optional modules it has switched on. Any member.

Studio-level facts live here and the user's own data lives in `/me`. The studio comes from the
verified membership, so there is no id in the path to get wrong.
